title: LEGO Art reveals 31221 Gustav Klimt – The Kiss, but does it beat the gold record?
summary: LEGO has officially unveiled a 4,000-piece LEGO Art recreation of Gustav Klimt's The Kiss, arriving 1 August, though it's not yet clear if it beats 31213 Mona Lisa's record for most metallic gold pieces in a set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO has officially unveiled 31221 Gustav Klimt – The Kiss, the latest addition to the LEGO Art theme. The 4,000-piece build releases on 1 August and recreates the famous Austrian painting using multiple metallic gold elements, echoing the Byzantine mosaic and Japanese lacquer techniques Klimt drew on for the original artwork.

What's still unconfirmed is exactly how many metallic gold pieces the set contains. That matters because LEGO Art has quietly built up a bit of a gold-piece leaderboard over the years. The soon-to-retire 31213 Mona Lisa currently holds the record with 314 metallic gold pieces out of 1,503 total, all used in the frame around Leonardo da Vinci's masterpiece. Before that, 2021's 76191 Infinity Gauntlet included 153 gold pieces, and 2020's 80012 Monkey King Warrior Mech had 119.

With The Kiss's much larger 4,000-piece count and gold being central to Klimt's original technique, there's plenty of reason to think it could challenge Mona Lisa's crown — but until LEGO confirms the breakdown, that's speculation.

## Why it matters
For collectors and display builders, metallic gold elements are prized both for their rarity and their striking look on a shelf. A new record-holder would be a notable moment for the LEGO Art theme and could affect demand and resale interest, especially with Mona Lisa retiring soon.

## What to watch next
Expect the full piece count and gold element breakdown to surface closer to or on the 1 August release date. Worth checking official LEGO channels or Brick Fanatics for confirmation before treating any gold-piece comparison as fact.

title: LEGO Ideas designer explains the story behind La Catrina set
summary: Ahead of its 1 August launch, LEGO designer Jim Clayton has spoken about the meaning behind the official LEGO Ideas La Catrina set and the Día de los Muertos celebration it represents.

Speaking at a roundtable interview attended by Brick Fanatics, Clayton explained that the 1,212-piece build was designed to reflect the true spirit of Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead), rather than the more macabre imagery some associate with Halloween.

Clayton said the team wanted the set to feel authentic to fans in Mexico while also helping introduce the holiday's meaning to a wider global audience. He highlighted the colourful floral details on La Catrina's dress as a nod to both craftsmanship and the celebration of loved ones who have passed.

La Catrina, the skeletal figure central to the design, originated as political satire by Mexican illustrator José Guadalupe Posada around 1910 before becoming a widely recognised cultural symbol.

The set is confirmed to launch on 1 August, and is described as the biggest LEGO Day of the Dead set to date.

## Why it matters
This is a notable release for LEGO Ideas fans, as it's one of the largest sets in that theme to draw on a specific cultural celebration. title: LEGO Ideas reveals why 21372 La Catrina ended up smaller than the original fan design

Designer Jim Clayton said he used other LEGO buildable figures as a starting point for sizing, before focusing heavily on the skull, which he described as the trickiest part to get right. He reportedly built more than 100 test versions of the skull, which is constructed partly upside down and then sandwiched together, before settling on a final approach that balanced detail, strength and buildability.

LEGO Ideas design manager Jordan David Scott also pointed to the figure's arms as a key factor. The original fan design relied on a support structure to hold certain poses, whereas the official LEGO set apparently took a different approach, which further influenced the overall scale of the finished model.

title: Rumoured LEGO Star Wars cinema set has a long line of LEGO movie theatres before it
summary: Chatter about a possible LEGO Star Wars cinema set for 2027 has us looking back at the LEGO cinemas that have already graced our shelves, from 2008's Town Plan to the beloved Palace Cinema modular.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has rounded up LEGO's cinema-building history following **rumours** (unconfirmed) of a new LEGO Star Wars cinema set, said to be numbered 75659 and dubbed a 'Movie Theatre'. According to these rumours, it would be an 18+ set retailing at $199.99 in the US and arriving on 1 April 2027 — but none of this has been officially confirmed by LEGO, so treat it as speculation for now.

If it does happen, it wouldn't be LEGO's first trip to the pictures. The first full LEGO cinema build appeared in **2008's 10184 Town Plan**, a 1,981-piece anniversary set marking 50 years of the LEGO brick, complete with a marquee, ticket booth, snack counter and a full screen showing a western.

The most famous LEGO cinema followed in **2013 with 10232 Palace Cinema**, a 2,196-piece modular building inspired by Hollywood's Chinese Theatre. It featured a four-walled interior with room for six minifigures at the screen, plus posters for in-universe films — and US buyers in September 2013 even got a bonus poster referencing The LEGO Movie.

A smaller entry came in **2014 with 40180 Bricktober Theater**, a 164-piece Toys 'R' Us giveaway set continuing the cinema theme on a much smaller scale.

## Why it matters
LEGO cinema builds have a strong pedigree among modular and city fans, so a potential Star Wars-themed entry — sitting alongside multi-theme sets like Friends, Batman and Icons — would be a notable addition if confirmed. For UK collectors and display builders, it's worth keeping an eye on official announcements before getting too invested in the rumoured details.
